evidence: Platts page 621 comparative sā like/resembling is explicitly derived through a Prakrit form from sadṛśa plus ka. It is distinct from the adjacent intensifying sā entry. CDIAL 13120 supplies the sadṛśa like family. These same responses are interpreted as comparative ek + sā/so/sī, preserving gender/vowel forms, spacing and regional pronunciation. The sadṛśa link records the base of the documented suffixed derivation, not an unsuffixed direct sound change. Local transmission is unresolved.
